doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: His father on the steamboats
summary: His father played piano on early river steamboats before settling in Rock Island; both parents died when Allred was young.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Didn’t your father play on steamboats?

My dad worked on the early versions of some of the steamboats, I think some early Streckfus stuff, but this had to be 1920. And unfortunately and sadly, my dad died when I was like eight years old you know. He never heard me play, never heard my son play, which if I have any regrets in my life that’s one of them. My mother died when I was eleven, but my sister was 20 years older than me, so she kind of gathered up some of my dad’s lore as far as the river. And he was just a punk kid but he was playing piano and he also played banjo and guitar because in his estimation, or in his words, the pianos were so bad on these boats that you really didn’t know what you were going to get. I mean he hopped from boat to boat and ended up having a sibling, a younger brother that I had never met and never been able to find, so that kept him out of the war, and he gravitated to Rock Island, Illinois, where there was, then, there was some music stuff going on with steamboats going across the river. So he gravitated there and met my mom, then I was born and so on and so forth. But I never really got to work with him, you know it’s sad.
It’s in your genes and you passed it on obviously.
